instructions: Peersus is a private Rust workspace (edition 2024, MSRV 1.96) for peer-to-peer file transfer with optional, separately installed extensions. Pull requests to `extension` are single-extension source submissions; pull requests to `main` change the host. Report only concrete, evidenced defects in behaviour, security or contracts, following .greptile/rules.md; skip style preferences and requests beyond the PR's stated scope.

rules.rule: The host never names a concrete extension: no extension name, ID, settings key, page or behaviour as a condition or special case. Extensions are identified by a host-assigned ID and everything they add is data rendered generically.

Every value from an extension or peer is untrusted: validate at the boundary, refuse explicitly when not understood, never unwrap/expect/panic on it, and never wait or loop without a bound on the main loop.
Extension calls, events, notifications, data and connections are rate limited and bounded; over the limit they are refused or deferred, never queued without bound.
unsafe is forbidden except in peersus-ui-android and peersus-plugin-android, where each block carries a // SAFETY: comment stating its invariant.
Secret text never reaches logs, diagnostics, accessibility trees, clipboard flows or error messages.
Unsupported capabilities and errors stay explicit: no fake fields, hidden no-ops, invented fallbacks or compatibility aliases without a real consumer.
Reuse the existing helper, component or path instead of adding a parallel one; do not merge distinct semantics into a flag-heavy abstraction.
Tests assert behaviour (state transitions, validation, errors, limits), not source strings, echoed fields or non-emptiness.

An extension submission changes exactly one extension directory, declares every permission it uses in its manifest, uses per-device permissions for peer actions, contains submission.toml, ownership.json and license notices, commits no build output, and its README states platforms and limitations honestly.

Untrusted extension source is built without secrets and validated on another runner; actions are pinned by full commit SHA; heavy jobs start only via the maintainer-applied run:ci label or manual dispatch; admission requires a pull_request run bound to the exact head commit. Flag anything exposing secrets to PR code, widening token permissions or letting contributors start paid runs.
